note: pcodec (codec 4) is reserved and not written by fstx 1.0: no file can hold it; the refusal is covered by reserved_codec4.fstx and reserved_pcodec.fstx in format-1.0.json. roundtrip_pyarrow: read_fstx() -> pyarrow.Table -> write_fstx(); roundtrip_pandas: the same through fstx.to_pandas() and a pandas DataFrame; roundtrip_polars: the same through fstx.to_polars() and a polars DataFrame, which carries no fstx metadata (DESIGN.md sections 2 and 4).

cases.about: logical, integer (INT_MAX, -INT_MAX, NA), double (NA, NaN, quiet NA = NA_real_ + 1, -0, Inf, -Inf, subnormal, max), character ("", NA, control characters)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical (the quiet NA 0x7FF80000000007A2 comes back as NA_real_ 0x7FF00000000007A2; identical() does not see payloads)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: not identical: to_pandas uses pandas' nullable dtypes, and a Float64 column cannot tell NaN from NA (pandas 3), so R's NaN comes back as NA

cases.about: no columns, no rows
every type with 0 rows (the schema alone: levels, ordered, time zone, integer64 class)
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: an empty polars Categorical has no levels and no order, and an empty Int64 comes back integer (int64 = 'auto')

cases.about: no columns but 5 rows (Arrow: a table of 5 rows and no columns)
every type all NA, 3 rows (a factor with levels and one with none)
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: an all-null polars Categorical has no levels, and an all-null Int64 comes back integer (int64 = 'auto')

cases.about: strings over 64 KB and over 2,000 bytes (given in the sidecar as byte count and md5)
600 distinct strings (FSST pages) and a 3-value column (dictionary pages: codes + dictionary)
Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Gujarati, Punjabi, Odia, Urdu, a ZWJ conjunct, the rupee sign, a 4-byte character; factor levels and a column name in Indian scripts
strings marked latin1 in R: stored as UTF-8 (R reads them back marked UTF-8; identical() still TRUE)
strings that are not valid UTF-8 (allowed by spec 9 rule 7; sidecar gives their bytes in hex)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: not identical by default: bad bytes become U+FFFD (identical only with invalid_utf8 = 'binary')

cases.about: bit64 integer64 (a double column with class integer64): big values, NA, and values whose bits are NA_real_, Inf or NaN (they must come back as numbers)
POSIXct in UTC, Asia/Kolkata (+05:30), America/New_York (DST), tzone "" and no tzone; whole, half and microsecond seconds, before 1970, 9999-12-31 23:59:59, NA
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical if the writer restores tzone "" vs none from the field metadata; both read as naive timestamp[us]
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical through to_pandas() with the metadata kept; tz "" vs none is lost without it
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: polars carries no metadata, so tzone "" and no tzone both come back as UTC

cases.about: POSIXct with sub-microsecond parts (as Sys.time() gives)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: not identical: timestamp[us] rounds to the microsecond (exact only with datetimes = 'float')

cases.about: POSIXct Inf, -Inf, NaN, NA (Arrow has only null); a POSIXct stored as integer (kept as an attribute blob, not natively)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: not identical: Inf, -Inf and NaN become null and come back NA (exact only with datetimes = 'float'); the integer POSIXct comes back as int32 storage only if the writer keeps phys from the metadata
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical (as pyarrow); the integer POSIXct comes back double

cases.about: Date stored as double (as.Date) and as integer, from year 1 to 9999, NA
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical if the writer restores double vs integer storage from the field metadata (date32 alone cannot tell)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical if dates stay datetime.date objects (pyarrow's default) and the metadata is kept; datetime64[ns] cannot hold years 1 and 9999
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: the integer Date comes back double (polars carries no metadata)

cases.about: fractional Dates, Inf, -Inf, NaN, NA
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: not identical: date32 floors fractions and makes Inf / NaN null (exact only with datetimes = 'float')

cases.about: factor with NA codes, with unused levels (kept), ordered factor, one level, Indian-script levels in a non-sorted order
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: a polars Categorical keeps only the levels in use, in order of first appearance, and no order

cases.about: factor with NA as a level (exclude = NULL): not stored natively (levels in the FXA1 blob); the NA-level code is a value, not a missing value
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical if the writer turns a null dictionary entry back into an NA level
cases.roundtrip_pandas: not identical: pandas categories cannot hold NA, so to_pandas turns the column into strings (with a warning)
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: to_polars turns the column into strings

cases.about: factor, Date and POSIXct with an extra class or a 2-value tzone: R stores them as plain int / double with the class in the attribute blob
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical if the class vector and blob travel in the field metadata
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical only if to_pandas keeps the metadata
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: classes kept in the attribute blob are lost (polars carries no metadata)

cases.about: difftime in every unit and hms (double + class + units in the attribute blob)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical (double with class and units in the metadata)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: not identical: the pandas Float64 column cannot tell NaN from NA (as basic), so the NaN in 'weeks' comes back NA; classes and units are kept
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: class and units are lost, the values come back as plain doubles

cases.about: column labels, units, a named-vector attribute, comment; table attributes (all in FXA1)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical if the blobs travel in the metadata
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical only if the metadata is kept
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: attributes are lost (polars carries no metadata)

cases.about: list-valued column and table attributes: stored with R serialize() (Python cannot decode them; it keeps the bytes)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical only if the opaque blobs are written back unchanged
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical only if the metadata is kept
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: attributes are lost (polars carries no metadata)

cases.about: character row names (pandas: the index)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical (row names in the table metadata)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical if to_pandas makes them the index and from_pandas stores a string index as row names
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: row names are lost (polars has no index)

cases.about: integer row names that are not automatic (x[c(4, 2), ] keeps 4, 2)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical (row names in the table metadata)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical if an integer index other than 0..n-1 becomes integer row names
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: row names are lost (polars has no index)

cases.about: data.table with a key (sorted) and a secondary index (index attribute with order vectors)
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: not identical: the Python writer drops the index (it cannot tell whether rows were reordered); the key is kept because k is still sorted
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: comes back a plain data.frame (class, key and index are lost)

cases.about: tibble class (tbl_df, tbl, data.frame)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical only if the metadata is kept
cases.roundtrip_polars: not identical: comes back a plain data.frame

cases.about: duplicate names, an empty name, spaces and punctuation, a Hindi name, the name "NA"
cases.roundtrip_pyarrow: identical (Arrow allows duplicate and empty names)
cases.roundtrip_pandas: identical (pandas allows duplicate names; selecting by a duplicate name gives both)
cases.roundtrip_polars: not written: polars refuses repeated column names (to_polars raises ValueError)

LZ4 block on every page

Zstandard level 19 on every page
